app.title: Manmen
app.description: Power settings, manuals, processes, and Docker cleanup from a GUI

pmset.title: Power settings (pmset)
pmset.description: Choose a power source, a setting, and a value. Administrator privileges are required.
pmset.adminNote: macOS shows an administrator authentication dialog on execute. Your password is never stored by the app.
pmset.remember: Skip password prompts (while the app is running)
pmset.rememberNote: Enter your password only once; subsequent runs need no password while the app is open. The password is never stored. After quitting, the credential expires with the normal timeout (about 5 minutes).
pmset.empty: Pick a setting and value, then run to see the result here.

pmsetSettings.proximitywake: wake when a nearby device is close
pmsetSettings.acwake: wake when the power source changes
pmsetSettings.destroyfvkeyonstandby: destroy the FileVault key on standby

man.title: Manual pages (man)
man.description: Pick a command from the list to display its manual page. No administrator privileges needed.
man.empty: Click a command in the list to show its manual here.

manAbout.title: About this command
manAbout.man: The standard macOS command for displaying online manuals (man man: display online manual documentation pages). Give it a command name to see its description, options, and examples.
manAbout.usage: Pick a command from the list above (e.g. pmset, caffeinate, launchctl) and press Show. Names not in the list (options, etc.) are rejected.

top.title: Process monitor (top)
top.description: Take a CPU / memory usage snapshot. No administrator privileges needed.
top.userInvalid: User names may contain only letters, digits, and . _ -
top.pidsInvalid: Enter up to 16 process IDs as integers separated by commas
top.statsHint: Leave everything unchecked to use top's default columns. Up to 16 columns.
top.note: Interactive mode is not supported, so this takes a one-shot snapshot in logging mode (-l 1). Treat %CPU in the first sample as approximate. Delay (-s) and repeated samples are not available.
top.hintSecondary: Breaks ties when the first key is equal. Leave blank to skip it.
top.hintCount: How many processes to list, from 1 to 100.
top.hintUser: Shows only processes owned by this user. Blank means everyone.
top.hintPids: Shows only these processes. Separate several IDs with commas.
top.hintNcols: Width of the log output. Too narrow drops columns from the table. Blank keeps top's default.
top.hintFrameworks: Leaves shared-library (framework) statistics out of the summary.
top.hintMemoryMap: Inspects each process's memory so sizes such as resident memory are numbers instead of N/A.
top.hintSwap: Adds swap, purgeable memory, and disk and network totals to the summary.
top.empty: Pick options and run to see the process list here.

topOrderHelp.default: Largest values first. This is top's default, passed as -o cpu with no prefix.
topOrderHelp.+: Smallest values first. The command becomes -o +cpu.
topOrderHelp.-: Largest values first, written explicitly as -o -cpu.

topModeHelp.n: CPU is a share since the previous sample. A single snapshot has little delta, so treat %CPU as approximate.
topModeHelp.a: Counts CPU and time cumulatively since top started.
topModeHelp.d: Counts only the change since the previous sample. Memory-map reporting is off unless you turn it on.

topHelp.pid: The number that identifies the process.
topHelp.command: The name of the running program.
topHelp.cpu: How much of the CPU the process is using.
topHelp.cpu_me: CPU time charged to this process by others.
topHelp.cpu_others: CPU time this process charged to others.
topHelp.csw: How many times the CPU switched to or from this process.
topHelp.time: Total CPU time used so far.
topHelp.threads: How many threads the process has.
topHelp.ports: How many Mach ports it holds.
topHelp.mregion: How many memory regions it has.
topHelp.mem: Physical memory the process is using.
topHelp.rprvt: Resident memory not shared with other processes.
topHelp.purg: Memory that can be discarded under pressure.
topHelp.vsize: Total virtual memory assigned to the process.
topHelp.vprvt: Address space private to the process.
topHelp.kprvt: Private memory held in the kernel.
topHelp.kshrd: Shared memory held in the kernel.
topHelp.pgrp: The process group this process belongs to.
topHelp.ppid: The process ID of the parent that started it.
topHelp.state: Current state, such as running or sleeping.
topHelp.uid: Numeric user ID of the owner.
topHelp.wq: Workqueue total and how many are running.
topHelp.faults: Times memory had to be fetched in (page faults).
topHelp.cow: Times memory was copied because it was written.
topHelp.pageins: Pages read from disk into memory.
topHelp.boosts: Times the process was temporarily raised in priority.
topHelp.cycles: CPU cycles spent running those instructions.
topHelp.jetpri: Jetsam priority: how likely the process is to be quit when memory is low.

topAbout.title: About this command
topAbout.top: The standard macOS command for displaying sorted process information (man top: display sorted information about processes). Sorting uses -o, the secondary key uses -O, and the count uses -n.
topAbout.usage: Choose sort, filters, counting, and columns, then press Snapshot. Only a single `top -l 1` run is executed. Delay (-s), interactive mode, and unknown keys are not accepted.

docker.title: Docker management (docker)
docker.description: Inspect containers, images, networks, volumes, disk usage, and build cache. No administrator privileges needed. All parsed from --format json into tables.
docker.pruneSummary: Open only when needed (pruning cannot be undone)
docker.name: Builder name
docker.nameInvalid: Builder names may contain only letters, digits, and . _ -
docker.hintName: Leave blank to inspect the current builder. Names starting with - are rejected.
docker.note: Pruning cannot be undone. Without --all only dangling cache is removed.
docker.hintForce: Remove without confirmation (-f). Turning it off may fail on the confirmation prompt.
docker.hintAll: Remove all unused cache (--all). Off means dangling cache only.
docker.noOptions: This subcommand takes no options. Just run it.
docker.empty: Pick a subcommand and run to see the result here.

dockerAbout.title: About this command
dockerAbout.docker: Inspects Docker state and prunes build cache (container ls -a / image ls / network ls / volume ls / system df / info / builder du, ls, inspect, version, prune). Reads parse --format json into tables and change nothing. Only prune deletes (-f / --all).
dockerAbout.usage: Pick a subcommand and press Run to inspect. Keep -f on and press Prune to delete. Turn --all on only to free a lot of space.

about.title: About this command
about.pmset: The standard macOS command for manipulating power management settings (man pmset: manipulate power management settings). It manages idle sleep timing, wake on network access, automatic restart on power loss, and more. Administrator (root) privileges are required to change settings.
about.sudo: sudo — run with administrator privileges. Required because changing pmset settings must be done as root.
about.scopes: -a applies to every power source. -b is battery only, -c is the power adapter only, and -u is UPS only.
about.value: setting and value — the chosen option and its value. Only 0/1, minutes (0–1440), or hibernatemode (0 / 3 / 25) are accepted. Immediate actions such as schedule or sleepnow are not available.
about.disablesleep: disablesleep — enable / disable system sleep (0 / 1). Shown as SleepDisabled in `pmset -g` output.
about.on: ON (1) — the system no longer sleeps automatically. Use for long tasks or presentations. Power usage and heat increase, so switch back OFF when done.
about.off: OFF (0) — return to normal sleep behavior. The system then sleeps according to timer settings such as sleep.

ui.stale: Options changed — run again to refresh

dockerSubHelp.prune: Delete build cache. Cannot be undone.
dockerSubHelp.containers: List containers (docker container ls -a), including stopped (read-only).
dockerSubHelp.sysdf: Show per-type disk usage (docker system df) (read-only).

dig.title: DNS lookup (dig)
dig.description: Look up IP addresses, mail servers, and more from domain names. No administrator privileges needed.
dig.name: Name
dig.nameInvalid: Enter a hostname using letters, digits, and . _ -
dig.serverInvalid: Enter an IP address or hostname for the server
dig.traceConflict: +trace cannot be combined with a server
dig.hintName: The domain name to look up. A trailing dot is allowed.
dig.hintIp: The IP address for reverse lookup, queried with -x.
dig.hintType: The record type. A is IPv4, AAAA is IPv6, MX is mail servers.
dig.hintClass: Leave as IN in most cases.
dig.hintServer: The DNS server to ask. Blank uses the macOS default. @ is added automatically.
dig.hintShort: Show only the answers, one per line (+short).
dig.hintTcp: Query over TCP (+tcp), useful when UDP is unreliable.
dig.hintTrace: Trace delegation from the root (+trace). Cannot be combined with a server.
dig.hintNoRecurse: Disable recursion (+norecurse), for checking authoritative answers.
dig.hintReverse: Look up the name for an IP (-x). Type and class are ignored while on.
dig.hintTransport: Whether to query over IPv4 or IPv6. Default is automatic.
dig.note: File input (-f), keys (-y / -k), and source address (-b) are not accepted. One lookup at a time.
dig.empty: Enter a name and run to see DNS answers here.

digAbout.title: About this command
digAbout.dig: The standard macOS command for querying DNS servers (man dig: DNS lookup utility). Find IPv4/IPv6 addresses (A / AAAA), mail servers (MX), name servers (NS), and more. Queries look like dig @server name type.
digAbout.usage: Enter a name, pick a type (A / MX, ...), and press Lookup. Fill in Server only to ask a specific server. Keep +short on to see just the answers.

ssh.title: SSH connection (ssh)
ssh.description: Inspect the effective config without connecting, or check connectivity only. No administrator privileges needed.
ssh.hostInvalid: Enter a hostname or IP using letters, digits, and . _ - :
ssh.userInvalid: User names may contain only letters, digits, and . _ -
ssh.hintDestination: A hostname, IP, or ~/.ssh/config alias. Aliases keep their IdentityFile and other settings. Do not use user@host form; put the user in its own field.
ssh.hintMode: Config inspection uses -G without connecting. Connectivity check runs only exit with BatchMode (no password prompts).
ssh.hintTimeout: Give up if there is no response within these seconds, from 5 to 30.
ssh.hintStrict: How to treat unknown hosts. no (disable verification) is not available.
ssh.hintVerbose: Show detailed connection logs with -v. Useful for diagnosing failures.
ssh.hintTransport: Whether to connect over IPv4 or IPv6. Default is automatic.
ssh.note: Interactive login, arbitrary remote commands, key files (-i), ProxyJump (-J), and forwarding (-L/-R/-D) are not accepted. Default keys and ssh-agent settings are used.
ssh.empty: Enter a destination and run to see the result here.
ssh.hintPurpose: Whether to inspect config, check connectivity, or open a tunnel.

sshAbout.title: About this command
sshAbout.ssh: The standard macOS command for securely connecting to remote hosts (man ssh: OpenSSH remote login client). -G shows the effective config without connecting; BatchMode=yes with exit checks connectivity without password prompts; -N opens a forwarding-only tunnel. The host field also accepts ~/.ssh/config aliases.
sshAbout.usage: Pick a purpose (inspect, connectivity, tunnel). Enter the destination by alias or free text, then press Run (Start tunnel for tunnels). Interactive login is not available.

sshTunnel.title: SSH tunnel (ssh -N)
sshTunnel.description: Start and stop forwarding-only SSH connections. No remote command is executed.
sshTunnel.hostInvalid: Enter a hostname or IP using letters, digits, and . _ - :
sshTunnel.userInvalid: User names may contain only letters, digits, and . _ -
sshTunnel.hintDirection: -L forwards local to remote, -R forwards remote to local, -D is a SOCKS proxy.
sshTunnel.hintBind: The address to listen on. LAN exposure (0.0.0.0, etc.) is rejected. Blank means 127.0.0.1.
sshTunnel.hintLocalPort: The local port to open. Starting fails if it is already in use.
sshTunnel.hintRemoteHost: Forward target host for -L/-R. For -L it is resolved from the jump host.
sshTunnel.hintDestination: The SSH server to go through. ~/.ssh/config aliases are selectable. Do not use user@host form; put the user in its own field.
sshTunnel.hintPort: SSH port of the jump host. Blank means 22.
sshTunnel.hintKeepalive: Send keepalive probes to hold idle connections (ServerAlive).
sshTunnel.hintTransport: Whether to connect over IPv4 or IPv6. Default is automatic.
sshTunnel.note: No password prompts appear (BatchMode). Key authentication must be ready. Remote commands and other options are not accepted.
sshTunnel.noteClose: Closing the app (window) stops all running tunnels. Nothing is left behind.
sshTunnel.empty: Start a tunnel to see the running list here.

sshTunnelAbout.title: About this command
sshTunnelAbout.tunnel: ssh -N opens forwarding without executing a remote command (man ssh -N: Do not execute a remote command). Supports -L (local to remote), -R (remote to local), and -D (SOCKS).
sshTunnelAbout.usage: Enter direction, ports, and jump host, then press Start tunnel. Press Stop in the list to close one. Closing the app stops every tunnel.

ps.title: Process list (ps)
ps.description: Take a snapshot of running processes. No administrator privileges needed.
ps.columnsHint: Pick at least one column. Up to 16 columns.
ps.hintSort: CPU order adds -r, memory order adds -m. None keeps ps default order.
ps.userInvalid: User names may contain only letters, digits, and . _ -
ps.pidsInvalid: Enter up to 16 process IDs as integers separated by commas
ps.hintUser: Shows only processes owned by this user. Blank means everyone.
ps.hintPids: Shows only these processes. Separate several IDs with commas.
ps.note: Always targets all processes (-A). The command column may contain spaces, so it stays last.
ps.empty: Pick options and run to see the process list here.

psHelp.pid: The number that identifies the process.
psHelp.ppid: The process ID of the parent that started it.
psHelp.pgid: The process group this process belongs to.
psHelp.%cpu: How much of the CPU the process is using.
psHelp.%mem: Share of physical memory in use.
psHelp.rss: Physical memory the process is using.
psHelp.vsz: Total virtual memory assigned to the process.
psHelp.time: Total CPU time used so far.
psHelp.etime: Time elapsed since the process started.
psHelp.state: Current state, such as running or sleeping.
psHelp.comm: The running program name, without arguments.
psHelp.command: The full command line including arguments.

psAbout.title: About this command
psAbout.ps: The standard macOS command for showing process status (man ps: process status). Columns use -o, CPU order uses -r, memory order uses -m, and filters use -U and -p.
psAbout.usage: Choose columns, sort, and filters, then press Snapshot. Unlike top this is a static one-shot list; treat %CPU as a lifetime average.

lsof.title: Open files (lsof)
lsof.description: Inspect files and connections held by processes. No administrator privileges needed.
lsof.pidsInvalid: Enter up to 16 process IDs as integers separated by commas
lsof.userInvalid: User names may contain only letters, digits, and . _ -
lsof.commInvalid: Command names may contain only letters, digits, and . _ -
lsof.portInvalid: Ports must be 1–65535, ranges as a-b
lsof.hostInvalid: Enter an IP address or hostname
lsof.stateConflict: State filtering is only available with TCP
lsof.stateLocked: State filtering is unavailable with UDP.
lsof.hintPids: Shows only these processes. Separate several IDs with commas.
lsof.hintUser: Shows only processes owned by this user. Blank means everyone.
lsof.hintProtocol: Protocol scope for the network filter.
lsof.hintPort: A single port or an a-b range. Blank means no restriction.
lsof.hintHost: An IP address or hostname. Blank means no restriction.
lsof.hintState: Filters by TCP connection state. Used together with -i.
lsof.note: Always runs with AND conditions (-a), no name resolution (-P -n), and full command names (+c 0). Large scans may take a while.
lsof.empty: Pick filters and run to see the result here.

lsofAbout.title: About this command
lsofAbout.lsof: The standard macOS command for listing open files and sockets (man lsof: list open files). Process filters use -p, -u, and -c; network filters use -i and -sTCP.
lsofAbout.usage: Pick at least one process or network filter, then press Snapshot. Protocol TCP with state LISTEN is the classic way to find listening ports.

whoami.title: Username (whoami)
whoami.description: Show the current username. No administrator privileges needed.
whoami.noOptions: This command takes no options. Just run it.
whoami.empty: Run to see the current username here.

whoamiAbout.heading: What is whoami
whoamiAbout.body: The standard macOS command that shows the current effective username (man whoami: display effective user id). Runs with no options.
whoamiAbout.usage: Just press Show. Options and arguments are not accepted.

who.title: Logged-in users (who)
who.description: Show who is logged in. No administrator privileges needed.
who.noOptions: This command takes no options. Just run it.
who.empty: Run to see the logged-in users here.

whoAbout.heading: What is who
whoAbout.body: The standard macOS command that shows who is logged in (man who: display who is logged in). Runs with no options.
whoAbout.usage: Just press Show. Options and arguments are not accepted.

w.title: Users and load (w)
w.description: Show logged-in users and a load summary. No administrator privileges needed.
w.noOptions: This command takes no options. Just run it.
w.empty: Run to see the users and load summary here.

wAbout.heading: What is w
wAbout.body: The standard macOS command that shows who is logged in and what they are doing (man w: display who is logged in and what they are doing). Runs with no options.
wAbout.usage: Just press Show. Options and arguments are not accepted.

sp.title: System info (system_profiler)
sp.description: Inspect hardware and software configuration, one data type at a time. No administrator privileges needed.
sp.note: One data type per run. Some types take a few seconds. Huge listings such as apps and fonts are unavailable.
sp.empty: Pick a data type and run to see system info here.

spTypeHelp.SPHardwareDataType: Model, chip, memory size, and other overview info.
spTypeHelp.SPSoftwareDataType: macOS version, uptime, and other overview info.

spAbout.heading: What is system_profiler
spAbout.body: The standard macOS command for reporting hardware and software configuration (man system_profiler: report system hardware and software configuration). With -json it returns machine-readable JSON. Pass one data type (e.g. SPHardwareDataType) per run.
spAbout.usage: Pick a data type and press Inspect. Results render as a collapsible tree; click to open deeper levels.

scutil.title: System config (scutil)
scutil.description: Inspect DNS, network state, and computer names. No administrator privileges needed. Nothing is changed.
scutil.empty: Pick a subcommand and run to see the result here.

scutilSubHelp.names: Show ComputerName, LocalHostName, and HostName (three --get runs).

scutilAbout.heading: What is scutil
scutilAbout.body: The standard macOS command for managing system configuration (man scutil: manage system configuration). This app only covers reads (--dns / --nwi / --get); writes such as --set are not accepted.
scutilAbout.usage: Pick a subcommand and press Inspect. Computer names cannot be changed here.

git.title: Git (git)
git.description: Inspect repository status, history, branches, and remotes. No administrator privileges needed. Nothing is changed.
git.hintDir: Pick a suggestion or type a path. Missing paths are rejected.
git.empty: Enter a directory and run to see the result here.

gitAbout.heading: What is git
gitAbout.body: The version control command (man git: the stupid content tracker). This app only covers reads (status / log / branch -a / remote -v); writes such as add, commit, and push are not accepted.
gitAbout.usage: Enter a repository directory, pick a subcommand, and press Inspect. Non-repository paths show git's error as-is.

ping.title: Ping (ping)
ping.description: Send ICMP echo requests to check reachability and latency. No administrator privileges required.
ping.hostInvalid: Enter a hostname or IP with alphanumerics and . _ - :
ping.hintHost: Hostname or IP address. Values starting with - are not allowed.
ping.hintCount: How many packets to send. Required because ping runs forever without it. 1–20.
ping.hintInterval: Seconds between packets. Fractional values allowed. Default is 1 second.
ping.hintTimeout: Abort after this many seconds. Empty means send the full count.
ping.hintWaitMs: Milliseconds to wait for each reply. Empty means the ping default.
ping.hintSize: Data bytes per packet. Default is 56.
ping.hintTtl: Packet time to live. Empty means the OS default.
ping.hintNumeric: Show numeric addresses without resolving names (-n).
ping.note: Flood (-f), sweeps, source selection (-S), and multicast-only options are not available.
ping.empty: Enter a host and run to see ping results here.

pingAbout.heading: What is ping
pingAbout.body: The standard macOS command that sends ICMP echo requests and waits for replies (man ping: send ICMP ECHO_REQUEST packets to network hosts). Shows reachability, round-trip time, and loss. Supports count (-c), interval (-i), timeout (-t), reply wait (-W), size (-s), TTL (-m), numeric (-n), and DF (-D).
pingAbout.usage: Enter a host and press Run. Unanswered packets are counted as timeouts in the loss rate.

curl.title: HTTP request (curl)
curl.description: Send a GET / HEAD request to a URL and inspect the status, headers, body, and timing. No administrator privileges required.
curl.urlInvalid: Enter a URL starting with http:// or https:// without spaces
curl.hintUrl: An http:// or https:// URL. Other schemes such as file:// are not allowed.
curl.hintMethod: GET fetches the body (headers shown with -i). HEAD fetches headers only (-I).
curl.hintHeaders: Headers to send, as "Name: value". Up to 5.
curl.hintFollow: Follow 3xx Location headers to the final response (-L).
curl.hintMaxRedirs: Maximum number of redirects to follow.
curl.hintMaxTime: Abort the whole transfer after this many seconds. Required so requests never hang.
curl.hintConnectTimeout: Seconds to wait for the connection. Empty means the curl default.
curl.hintHttpVersion: Force an HTTP version. Auto lets negotiation decide.
curl.hintIpVersion: Force connecting over IPv4 or IPv6.
curl.hintCompressed: Request a compressed response and decompress it (--compressed).
curl.hintInsecure: Skip certificate verification (-k). Use only for testing.
curl.note: Uploads (-d/-F/-T), saving to files (-o/-O), config files (-K), and cookie/auth options are not available. Only the first 64 KB of the body is shown.
curl.empty: Enter a URL and run to see the response here.

curlAbout.heading: What is curl
curlAbout.body: The standard macOS command for transferring data from a URL (man curl: transfer a URL). Shows the HTTP status code, response headers, and body, plus how long DNS, connect, TLS, and the first byte took.
curlAbout.usage: Enter a URL and press Run. Turn on "Follow redirects (-L)" to see the final destination.
curlAbout.safety: In addition to the command shown, it always runs with -q (ignore ~/.curlrc), -g (disable URL globbing), --proto / --proto-redir (http/https only), --max-filesize (stop downloads over 20 MB), and -w (to collect timing).

curlResult.binary: The body is binary and is not shown
curlResult.truncated: The body is long; only the first 64 KB is shown

kill.title: Send signal (kill)
kill.description: Send a signal to processes to terminate, pause, or resume them. Other users' processes require administrator privileges.
kill.pidsInvalid: Enter up to {{max}} numeric PIDs separated by commas or spaces (0 and 1 are not allowed)
kill.hintPids: PIDs to signal. Use PIDs found with ps / top / lsof. Up to {{max}}.
kill.hintTargets: What each PID currently is, according to ps. Always check before sending.
kill.hintSudo: Use for root or other users' processes. You may be asked to authenticate.
kill.note: PID 0 (whole process group), 1 (launchd), and this app itself cannot be signaled. kill -l and numeric signals are not available.
kill.empty: Enter PIDs and send to see the results here.

killSignalHelp.TERM: A normal termination request (kill's default). The process can clean up before exiting. Try this first.
killSignalHelp.INT: An interrupt, the same as Ctrl+C.
killSignalHelp.HUP: Hang-up. Daemons often treat it as "reload configuration".
killSignalHelp.QUIT: A quit request, the same as Ctrl+\. May leave a crash report (core dump).
killSignalHelp.KILL: Force kill. The process cannot refuse or clean up, and unsaved data is lost. Use only when TERM does not work.
killSignalHelp.STOP: Pause the process. It cannot be refused. Resume with CONT.
killSignalHelp.CONT: Resume a process paused with STOP.

killAbout.heading: What is kill
killAbout.body: The standard macOS command for sending signals to processes (man kill: terminate or signal a process). Despite the name, it can also pause (STOP), resume (CONT), and reload (HUP).
killAbout.usage: Enter PIDs found with ps / top / lsof, check the target processes, then press Review and Send. Send TERM first and use KILL only if the process does not stop.
killAbout.safety: Signals are sent only from the button in the confirmation panel; ⌘↵ just opens the panel. PID 0, 1, and this app itself are rejected, and only 7 common signals are available.

killResult.hint: A successful send does not mean the process exits immediately. Check the target processes list to see if it is still running.

traceroute.title: Route trace (traceroute)
traceroute.description: Find the routers (hops) on the way to a host and the round-trip time to each. No administrator privileges required.
traceroute.firstTtlInvalid: First hop must be between 1 and max hops
traceroute.worst: Worst case if nothing replies: about {{secs}} s (limit {{max}} s)
traceroute.worstInvalid: Worst case would be about {{secs}} s. Reduce hops, probes, or wait (limit {{max}} s)
traceroute.hintProtocol: UDP is the default. If the trace stops partway, ICMP (-I) may get through.
traceroute.hintMaxTtl: How many hops to trace. Stops early when the host is reached.
traceroute.hintFirstTtl: Which hop to start from. Use it to skip your home or office network.
traceroute.hintWait: Seconds to wait for each reply.
traceroute.hintNumeric: Show IP addresses without resolving names (-n). Finishes faster.
traceroute.hintAsLookup: Look up each hop's AS number, i.e. which organization's network it is (-a).
traceroute.note: Low-level options such as source selection (-s/-i), gateways (-g), bypassing routing (-r), and firewall evasion (-e) are not available.
traceroute.empty: Enter a host and run to see the route here.

tracerouteAbout.heading: What is traceroute
tracerouteAbout.body: The standard macOS command that shows the path packets take to a host (man traceroute: print the route packets take to network host). It sends packets with increasing TTL and uses the errors routers return to map the route and the time to each hop.
tracerouteAbout.usage: Enter a host and press Run. Use it to find where traffic stops when ping fails, or which segment is slow. * means no reply, but many routers are configured not to reply, so it is not always a failure.

tracerouteResult.hint: !H, !N, etc. are unreachable notices (!H: host, !N: network, !X: administratively prohibited).

palette.title: Command search
palette.placeholder: Search by command or feature (e.g. ping, process)
palette.help: ↑↓ to select · Enter to open · Esc to close

disk.pathInvalid: Enter a path starting with / or ~ without line breaks

df.title: Disk free (df)
df.description: Show the size, usage, and free space of each mounted volume. No administrator privileges required.
df.hintPath: When set, only the volume containing this path is shown.
df.hintFsType: Filter by file system type. apfs is the Mac's internal disk; msdos/exfat are USB drives and similar.
df.hintLocal: Only volumes attached to this Mac, excluding network drives (-l).
df.hintAll: Include mounts that are normally hidden (-a).
df.hintHideSystem: Hide internal macOS volumes such as /System/Volumes/VM and simulators. The command does not change.
df.note: Always fetched with -k (KB), -Y (type), and -i (inodes); units are converted on screen.
df.empty: Run to see free space for each volume here.

dfAbout.heading: What is df
dfAbout.body: The standard macOS command that shows free disk space (man df: display free disk space). Shows each volume's size, usage, free space, capacity, and inode usage.
dfAbout.usage: Press Run to list all volumes. On APFS, volumes in the same container share free space, so several rows show the same free value. Use du to find what is using the space.

dfResult.hint: Capacity turns yellow at 85% and red at 95%. APFS volumes share free space within a container.

du.title: Folder usage (du)
du.description: Measure how much space each folder uses, largest first. No administrator privileges required.
du.hintPath: Folder to measure. Starts with / or ~.
du.hintDepth: How many levels to list. 0 shows only the total; 1 shows each subfolder.
du.hintAllFiles: List files as well as folders (-a).
du.hintOneFs: Do not descend into other volumes such as external disks (-x).
du.hintApparent: Count apparent file size instead of actual disk usage (-A). Differs for compressed or sparse files.
du.hintTimeout: Stop after this many seconds and show what was counted so far. This is an app limit, not a du option.
du.note: Returns up to 1000 entries, largest first. Following symlinks (-H/-L) and exclude patterns (-I) are not available.
du.empty: Enter a path and run to see the largest folders here.

duAbout.heading: What is du
duAbout.body: The standard macOS command that shows disk usage of files and folders (man du: display disk usage statistics). It walks folder contents to add them up, so large folders take time.
duAbout.usage: When df shows little free space, measure ~ at depth 1, then drill into large folders. Folders you lack permission for can be counted after granting this app Full Disk Access in System Settings.

duResult.timedOut: Stopped at the time limit; results are partial and the total was not counted. Reduce depth or raise the limit.
duResult.errors: {{n}} item(s) could not be read (e.g. permission denied) and are not included in the total.
duResult.truncated: Too many entries; showing the largest {{n}}

ifconfig.title: Network interfaces (ifconfig)
ifconfig.description: Show this Mac's IP addresses, MAC addresses, and the state of each interface. No administrator privileges required.
ifconfig.interfaceInvalid: Enter an interface name like en0 (lowercase letters and digits)
ifconfig.hintInterface: Name an interface such as en0 to show only it. Empty shows all (-a).
ifconfig.hintActiveOnly: Only list interfaces whose link is active or that have an address. The command does not change.
ifconfig.note: Display only. Setting addresses, up/down, and creating/destroying interfaces are not available.
ifconfig.empty: Run to see each interface's addresses here.

ifconfigAbout.heading: What is ifconfig
ifconfigAbout.body: The standard macOS command for showing and changing network interface settings (man ifconfig: configure network interface parameters). This app only shows them. On most Macs en0 is Wi-Fi, lo0 is the Mac itself (127.0.0.1), and utun is a tunnel such as a VPN.
ifconfigAbout.usage: Press Run to see interfaces in use and their IP addresses. Which interface is Wi-Fi is labeled automatically from networksetup. Check DNS and proxy settings with networksetup.

ifconfigResult.hint: /24 etc. is the netmask length. Gray IPv6 addresses (fe80::) are link-local, used only within the local network.

networksetup.title: Network settings (networksetup)
networksetup.description: Show network services, DNS and proxy settings, Wi-Fi state, and more. No administrator privileges required.
networksetup.devicePlaceholder: Detect Wi-Fi automatically when empty (e.g. en0)
networksetup.deviceInvalid: Enter a device name like en0 (lowercase letters and digits)
networksetup.hintService: The services listed in System Settings > Network.
networksetup.hintDevice: The Wi-Fi device name. When empty, it is found from the Wi-Fi hardware port.
networksetup.note: Only -get / -list commands are available. Changing DNS or proxies, switching locations, and other -set commands are not.
networksetup.empty: Choose what to show and run to see the settings here.

networksetupSubHelp.services: Network services in priority order (-listnetworkserviceorder). Services higher in the list are preferred.
networksetupSubHelp.info: IP settings, DNS servers, search domains, and proxies for the chosen service (-getinfo and 8 more commands).
networksetupSubHelp.wifi: Wi-Fi power and the current network name (-getairportpower / -getairportnetwork).
networksetupSubHelp.locations: The current network location and all saved locations (-getcurrentlocation / -listlocations).

networksetupAbout.heading: What is networksetup
networksetupAbout.body: The standard macOS command for viewing and changing System Settings > Network from the command line (man networksetup: configuration tool for network settings in System Preferences). This app only uses its read commands.
networksetupAbout.usage: Choose what to show and press Run. If Service details shows no DNS servers, DNS is provided automatically (e.g. by your router). The DNS actually in use can also be checked with scutil --dns.

networksetupResult.wifiHint: The network name may be unavailable even when connected, because macOS hides Wi-Fi names without Location Services permission.
